coverage.evidence: m3_naming.py built all 82 entities (sensor 62, binary_sensor 6, button 6, switch 6, climate 1, datetime 1) through each platform's real async_setup_entry over all 5 coordinator_scenarios(); sorted every entity_id (per platform and global) and every display name in en/sv/de; compared every leaf of strings.json with de/en/sv (keys, placeholders, en values); checked ENUM option state strings. entity.py examined as the base (translation_key/entity_id assignment) through the built entities.

findings.title: German run-optimization refusal names {entry_id}; production passes {entry_ids}, so the de message cannot render
findings.claim: translations/de.json exceptions.run_optimization_no_prices.message uses placeholder {entry_id} while strings.json, sv.json and both raise sites pass only entry_ids, so 1 of 3 shipped languages cannot format the message the optimize_now button raises.
findings.mechanism: button.py ForceOptimizationButton.async_press (and services.py run_optimization) raise HomeAssistantError(translation_key='run_optimization_no_prices', translation_placeholders={'entry_ids': ...}); the de string formats {entry_id}. str.format raises KeyError; Home Assistant's translation loader validates a localized string's placeholders against the English one and discards a mismatching one, so German users get the English text (plus a load-time error log) instead of German.

evidence.machine: macOS arm64, orchestrator box (local seat B5)
evidence.contention_note: shared box, other finder seats running; count is contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-de: in memory, '{entry_id}' -> '{entry_ids}' in the de message

findings.metric_definition: shipped languages whose exceptions.<key>.message raises KeyError when formatted with the placeholders on the HomeAssistantError production raises
findings.phenomenon_property: Every leaf string of every translations/<lang>.json carries exactly the {placeholder} set of the same leaf in strings.json.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: translations/de.json: {entry_id} -> {entry_ids} in exceptions.run_optimization_no_prices.message; plus a tests/entities.py check that every translation leaf's placeholder set equals strings.json's (the existing strings/translation drift check compares keys, not placeholders).

findings.title: Declared 'lifetime' family sorts as 3 runs by sensor entity_id (cost_total_heating, space_heating_*, total_energy)
findings.claim: The four sensors const.ENTITY_FAMILY_OVERRIDES declares as family 'lifetime' suggest entity ids sensor.heat_pump_optimizer_{cost_total_heating, space_heating_cost, space_heating_energy, total_energy}, which sort into 3 separate runs among the sensor ids; every other declared family is one run per platform.
findings.mechanism: #1668 moved the four meters' display names to lead with 'Lifetime' and declared the family via overrides, but left translation keys (from which the suggested object id is built) untouched, so the id sort keeps the old cost_/space_/total_ placement. The name sort is contiguous in en/sv/de (0 excess runs).

findings.proposed_fix_scope: New installs only, the #1227/#1333 pattern: suggested ids for the four meters gain the lifetime_ lead (unique ids unchanged, so existing installs keep their ids and history), or an owner ruling that a declared family is a name-sort family only, recorded beside ENTITY_FAMILY_OVERRIDES. Docs/card references to these ids need the legacy-fallback treatment.

leads.what: The M3 universe lists binary_sensor, button, climate, entity, sensor, switch .py but not custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/datetime.py, which ships the away_return entity (family 'away'); this seat measured it through the rig anyway, outside the enumerated cells.
Second raise site of the same exception key as D8-s2-01; the de translation fix covers it, but the services path was not driven by a harness here.
